openings.name: Italian Game
openings.summary: Quick development, bishop aimed at f7, then a slow build-up with c3 and d3.
ideas: Develop knights and bishops before moving the queen.
The bishop on c4 eyes the weak f7 square.
c3 prepares a later d4 to take the centre.

notes.2: Develop with a threat: the e5 pawn is attacked.
notes.4: The Italian bishop aims at f7, the weakest square near the black king.

notes.10: Castle early to bring the king to safety and the rook toward the centre.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
openings.summary: Offer the c-pawn to deflect Black from the centre; develop naturally and pressure d5.
ideas: c4 challenges the d5 pawn from the side.
Bg5 pins the knight that defends d5.

openings.name: Scandinavian Defence
openings.summary: Challenge e4 at once; the queen recaptures and retreats to a5 with quick development.
ideas: One clear plan from move one.
The queen on a5 pins the c3 knight against nothing but stays active.
Develop the light bishop outside the pawn chain before e6.

notes.9: Bring the bishop out before playing e6.

openings.name: French Defence
openings.summary: A solid pawn chain with e6 and d5; Black counter-attacks the centre with c5 and f6 later.
ideas: e6 and d5 form a solid chain.
Attack White's pawn chain at its base with c5.
The light-squared bishop is Black's problem piece.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez
openings.summary: Pressure on the knight that defends e5; a rich, strategic game with long-term pressure.
ideas: Bb5 attacks the defender of e5.
Keep the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal.
c3 and d4 build a big centre.

openings.name: London System
openings.summary: A reliable set-up: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nd2, Bd3. Plans matter more than move orders.
ideas: Develop the dark bishop before e3 locks it in.
A solid triangle of pawns on c3, d4, e3.
Later Ne5 and a kingside attack.

notes.8: Support d4 against the c5 attack.

notes.12: Keep the bishop rather than allow a trade on f4.
notes.14: Aim the bishop at the black king.

openings.name: English Opening
openings.summary: A reversed Sicilian: control d5 from the side and fianchetto the king's bishop.
ideas: Control d5 from the flank.
The g2 bishop pressures the long diagonal.
Flexible: transposes to many structures.

openings.name: Sicilian Najdorf
openings.summary: The sharpest answer to e4: imbalance the centre and counter-attack on the queenside.
ideas: c5 fights for d4 from the side.
Black gets the half-open c-file.
a6 controls b5 and prepares b5 expansion.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defence
openings.summary: Solid like the French, but the light bishop gets out before e6.

openings.name: King's Indian Defence
openings.summary: Let White build a centre, then attack it with e5 and a kingside pawn storm.
ideas: Fianchetto and castle quickly.
Strike back with e5 or c5.

openings.name: Slav Defence
openings.summary: Defend d5 with c6, keeping the light bishop free; a rock-solid answer to the Queen's Gambit.
ideas: c6 supports d5 without blocking the bishop.
